title: Lay three floorboards tight together, leaving a 10-20 mm expansion gap at each wall
instruction: Lay the three brown floorboards flat in the walled bay, side by side across it, starting along the far wall. Leave a gap of 10 to 20 mm between the boards and each of the three walls, and push the boards tight against each other.
context: Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031, whose work includes hardwood floors) and floor fitters lay wood and laminate floors with an expansion gap at every wall, commonly 10 to 15 mm and later hidden by the skirting board, because wood swells with the humidity: a floor laid tight against a wall buckles or lifts when it swells. The boards themselves go tight together, closed up with a tapping block or a pull bar, so no joint stays open. Doing both at once is the skill: each new board is set down short of the last and pushed home against it without driving the floor into the far wall, and each stays centred between the side walls. Here three short boards (300 mm; the gap kept at its real size) go across a 330 mm bay, so a board is within 10 to 20 mm of both side walls only within 5 mm of centred.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Two kinds of thing are on the table. (1) The bay: three fixed walls of grey-painted plywood, each 20 mm thick and 40 mm tall, fastened to the table. The left wall runs along x from x 16.0 to 36.0 cm with its inside face at y +16.5 cm (it spans y +16.5 to +18.5 cm); the right wall is its mirror image, its inside face at y -16.5 cm; the far wall runs along y from y -18.5 to +18.5 cm with its inside face at x 36.0 cm (it spans x 36.0 to 38.0 cm), closing the far ends of both side walls. The bay between them is 330 mm wide (along y) and 200 mm deep (along x, from its open edge at x 16.0 cm, level with the side walls' near ends, to the far wall); it is open toward the arms and its floor is the table. (2) Floorboards: three loose, identical pine boards stained dark brown, each 300 mm long, 50 mm wide and 16 mm thick, 0.11 kg, plain rectangular blocks with flat faces and square edges (no tongue, groove or click joint); a board's two 300 x 50 mm faces are alike. They lie flat on the table outside the bay on a 300 x 50 mm face with their length along x, centred at x 25.0 cm and y +23.5 cm (board a), x 25.0 cm and y +31.0 cm (board b) and x 25.0 cm and y -23.5 cm (board c): two in front of the left arm, one in front of the right arm. Laid side by side across the bay and tight together, the three boards make a floor 150 mm deep, leaving 50 mm of the bay's depth for the far gap and the strip at the open edge; a board laid centred across the bay is 15 mm from each side wall. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state from the boards' poses (in a real trial: a steel rule, feeler gauges and a top photo). A board's 'outline' is its shadow seen from above. A board is 'pinned' when its lowest point is at most 42 mm above the table (the walls' height plus 2 mm) and its outline comes within 3 mm of a wall's inside face or crosses it (touching a wall, leaning on one or lying on its top); the walls' outside faces do not count. A board is 'laid' when it lies flat on the floor (its broad faces tilted at most 3 degrees from level, its lowest point at most 2 mm above the table), its length seen from above is within 3 degrees of y (across the bay), its outline is inside the bay (x 16.0 to 36.0 cm), and both its end gaps, from its outline to the left and to the right wall's inside face along y, are 10 to 20 mm. The 'far gap' is the distance along x from the outline of the laid board nearest the far wall to the far wall's inside face. A 'joint' is the gap along x between the outlines of two neighbouring laid boards (in order of distance from the far wall), read on the lines y +14.0 cm and y -14.0 cm (10 mm in from a centred board's ends); the wider reading counts. A gripper's 'finger zone' is every point within a set radius of the line from the point between its finger tips to 38 mm back up the gripper; the radius reaches a finger's outer corner whichever way the gripper is turned: the square root of (half the finger gap + 10 mm)^2 + (20 mm)^2, so 60 mm fully open and 22 mm closed. 'Hands off' means both finger zones are at least 30 mm from every board. Score 0 if any board is pinned. Otherwise: 1.0 if all three boards are laid, the far gap is 10 to 20 mm, both joints are 3 mm or less and hands are off; else 0.25 for each laid board: 0.75 when all three are laid but a joint is over 3 mm, the far gap is under 10 or over 20 mm, or hands are not off (a finger zone under 30 mm from a board); 0.5 for two laid boards; 0.25 for one; 0 for none (boards left outside the bay, on an edge, on top of another board, turned more than 3 degrees, or under 10 or over 20 mm from a side wall). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Any board may go in any place, and boards that are not laid count only for the pinned rule. Limits are inclusive. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held for 1 s with neither end of any board moving more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, hands off is taken as met.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with the simulator's default friction on the bare table (no underlay); the walls are fixed. The boards are short (300 mm, about a fifth of a real board) and plain-edged (no tongue and groove or click joint), so joints are closed by pushing the boards together; the 10-20 mm expansion gap is kept at its real size. The scorer reads the boards' poses and each gripper's finger-tip point, tool point and opening (no heading), so each finger zone is round.
reset_notes: Put the three boards back flat on the table with their length along x, centred at x 25.0 cm and y +23.5 cm, x 25.0 cm and y +31.0 cm, and x 25.0 cm and y -23.5 cm. The walls are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
